zh-CN.photos.album.beijing-memory.title: 北京记忆
北京市房山区河北镇河南村。名字很有意思的地方。此地在大石河上游，霞云岭以东，房山城关以北，比较偏远。当地多老人，生活节奏慢，这方面像河北；但公交方便，基础设施好，居民也都是北京户口，退休工资高，这些元素让人感觉仍在北京。
宛平城外，卢沟桥边，夕阳西下，永定河美景。
夕阳西下，右侧是社科大的新教学楼，左侧是新楼的建造基地，基地的蓝色铁墙外，是盛开的向日葵。向日葵不知是自然生长的，还是有心人特意种的。
北京站前有各式各样的人，有人缓步行走尽显疲惫，有人接打电话满脸笑意。两位游客正蹲着和一位清洁工交谈。再过一分钟就是18点整，北京站将响起《东方红》的旋律。
小清河公园在社科大东1公里左右，当时经常来这散步，图为小清河公园雪景。
皮村街景，典型的北京城中村，低矮的平房和装修简单的店面。街上多北方美食，也有很多川菜。皮村东边是温榆河，我当时住在南边的通州。
温榆河景，前方是铁路。左岸是我当时住的地方，右岸有通州北关、物资学院等，再过一条小河就是万达广场。
zh-CN.photos.album.malaysia-snapshots.title: 大马随拍
泼水节，柏威年商场前的大路被封，路中间搭了个舞台。晚上举办活动，人山人海，先是唱歌，再是泼水，最后大家一起跳舞，相当于露天蹦迪。外国人容易激动，跳的很开心，我比较内向，在人群中瑟瑟发抖。
中午很热，但黑风洞仍然人潮汹涌。从半山腰往下看，可以看到楼梯上努力攀爬的游客，可以看到广场上星罗密布的人点，还可以看到印度神像的高大背影。中国游客最多，其次是印度的参拜者。印度人大多光着脚，走一段路还会参拜一下。此地猴多，但这张照片没出镜。
武吉免登是吉隆坡最繁华的旅游目的地之一，美食街人山人海，挤满了世界各地的游客。美食街多为东南亚和中国美食。美食街入口有时会遇到巴勒斯坦的难民乞讨者——作为穆斯林国家，马来西亚对全世界穆斯林来说也是很好的居住地。
吉隆坡武吉免登美食街
吉隆坡武吉免登美食街
康乐夜市是吉隆坡较大的夜市，每周三开放，位置在吉隆坡东南郊区。夜市旁边是思特雅大学（UCSI），这个学校2026年qs排名全球第269名。从qs排名来看，在北理工（第259名）和中山大学（第276名）之间。
彼时我们来早了，夜市还没有多少人，很多商家在做最后的准备。夜市多是大马华人和中国大陆的美食，比如椰子水、凉茶、盐焗螃蟹、蚝煎、安顺猪肠粉、长沙臭豆腐、江西酱香饼、衢州鸭货、福鼎肉片，也有其他民族的美食，比如五花肉卷火鸡面/泡菜、泰国猪脚面、章鱼小丸子、沙嗲烧烤。还有热量炸弹炸菠萝蜜。

en.photos.album.beijing-memory.title: Beijing Memories
Henan Village, Hebei Town, Fangshan District, Beijing—a place with an interesting name. It is in the upper reaches of the Dashi River, east of Xiayunling and north of Fangshan’s old town, and is fairly remote. Many residents are older, and life moves slowly; in that respect it feels like Hebei Province. Yet convenient buses, good infrastructure, Beijing household registration, and high pensions make it feel unmistakably part of Beijing.
Henan Village in Hebei Town, Fangshan District, Beijing
Outside Wanping Fortress, beside Lugou Bridge: sunset and a beautiful view of the Yongding River.
Sunset by Lugou Bridge and the Yongding River
At sunset, the new teaching building of the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences is on the right, and the construction site for a new building is on the left. Sunflowers bloom outside the site’s blue metal fence. I do not know whether they grew naturally or someone planted them with care.
University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Fangshan, Beijing
Sunflowers outside a blue construction fence at the university
A glimpse of the Great Wall at Badaling.
A glimpse of the Great Wall at Badaling
All sorts of people gather outside Beijing Railway Station. Some walk slowly, visibly tired; others smile as they make or answer calls. Two visitors are squatting to talk with a cleaner. In one minute it will be exactly 18:00, and the station will play the melody of “The East Is Red.”
Beijing Railway Station, Dongcheng District, Beijing
Xiaoqing River Park is about one kilometer east of the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. I often came here for walks at the time. This is the park in the snow.
Xiaoqing River Park in the snow
A street in Picun, a typical urban village in Beijing, with low single-story houses and simply fitted shops. The street has plenty of northern Chinese food and many Sichuan dishes too. The Wenyu River lies east of Picun; I was living to the south, in Tongzhou, at the time.
A street in Picun with low houses and shops
A view of the Wenyu River, with a railway ahead. I was living on the left bank at the time. On the right bank are Tongzhou Beiguan and Beijing Wuzi University, among other places; across another small river is Wanda Plaza.
The Wenyu River with a railway ahead
en.photos.album.malaysia-snapshots.title: Snapshots of Malaysia
For the water festival, the main road in front of Pavilion was closed and a stage set up in the middle. The evening event drew a huge crowd: first singing, then splashing water, and finally everyone dancing together—an open-air dance party. The foreigners were easily carried away and danced happily. Being rather introverted, I stood trembling in the crowd.
A water festival outside Pavilion Kuala Lumpur
It was hot at midday, but Batu Caves was still packed. Looking down from halfway up, I could see visitors working their way up the stairs, people scattered like dots across the square, and the towering back of the Hindu statue. Chinese tourists were the largest group, followed by Indian worshippers. Most of the Indians were barefoot and stopped to pray along the way. There are many monkeys here, but none appear in this photo.
The stairs, square, and statue at Batu Caves
Bukit Bintang is one of Kuala Lumpur’s busiest tourist destinations. The food street is packed with visitors from around the world and mostly offers Southeast Asian and Chinese food. At the entrance, one sometimes encounters Palestinian refugees begging. As a Muslim country, Malaysia is also an attractive place to live for Muslims from around the world.
Bukit Bintang food street, Kuala Lumpur
A busy food street in Bukit Bintang
Taman Connaught Night Market is one of Kuala Lumpur’s larger night markets. It opens every Wednesday in the city’s southeastern suburbs. Beside it is UCSI University, ranked 269th worldwide in the 2026 QS rankings, between Beijing Institute of Technology at 259th and Sun Yat-sen University at 276th.
We arrived early, when there were still few people and many vendors were making their final preparations. Much of the food is Malaysian Chinese or from mainland China: coconut water, herbal tea, salt-baked crab, oyster omelets, Teluk Intan chee cheong fun, Changsha stinky tofu, Jiangxi savory pancakes, Quzhou duck snacks, and Fuding pork slices. There is food from other communities too, including pork-belly rolls with Buldak noodles or kimchi, Thai pork-knuckle noodles, takoyaki, and satay. There is also the calorie bomb of deep-fried jackfruit.
Taman Connaught Night Market, Kuala Lumpur
Taman Connaught Night Market before the evening crowds
